title: Initiative Commitment Currency and Cross-Org OKR Alignment Pilot
creator: Priya Raman
description:
Purpose: Pilot a lightweight, quantifiable mechanism to align company-level OKRs with cross-functional initiatives by introducing a 'Commitment Currency'—a simple token representing committed engineering/product capacity (slice of team sprint capacity) tied to initiative outcomes. The goal is to reduce ambiguous ownership, speed up dependency resolution, and improve trade-off conversations when capacity shifts are requested.

Scope: This pilot covers three cross-functional initiatives spanning Serving Runtime, Console observability, and Dedicated capacity policy work. We will run the pilot with 6 engineering teams, Product, Design, and Infra SRE. It includes:
- Definition and ledger for Commitment Currency tokens.
- Initiative tagging matrix (OKR -> initiatives -> owners) surfaced in the Console and PM dashboard.
- A lightweight gating flow for cross-team trade-offs (request -> negotiator -> commit).
- Retrospective and metrics collection after one cycle.

Out of scope: Full org-wide enforcement, billing/financialization of tokens, automated enforcement in CI.

Context/Why now: Recent quarterly reviews surfaced repeated ambiguity about which initiatives absorb overflow capacity when company-level priorities shift. PMs and Eng leads report 10+ days of discussion per dependency before a decision; escalations to execs are increasing. The Commitment Currency is intended to create a common language for capacity commitments that is actionable during planning and mid-cycle re-prioritization.
acceptance_criteria: Commitment Currency spec published and reviewed by Eng, PM, Design (Confluence link).
Pilot ledger implemented as a lightweight Google Sheet and mirrored into the Pilot Dashboard with per-initiative token counts.
OKR -> Initiative matrix view available in the PM Console (read-only) and linked from the company OKR page.
Gating flow documented and at least two inter-team trade-off requests executed using the flow.
Post-pilot retrospective held with measurable outcomes and proposed production rollout plan.
success_metrics: Reduce average dependency decision lead time from ~10 days to <=3 days during the pilot window.
Increase clarity of OKR ownership: >=90% of company-level OKR sub-initiatives have a named owner and token commitment.
No regression in quarterly delivery milestones attributable to the pilot (tracked in roadmap).
rollout_plan: Week 0: Finalize spec and comms. Week 1: Onboard pilot teams and populate ledger. Week 2-4: Run pilot during one sprint cycle; collect data. Week 5: Retro and decision (rollback, iterate, or expand). If metrics hit threshold, prepare production proposal for Q3. Owners will produce a short runbook for next cycle and an engineering artifact request if automation is recommended.
